status: pre-registered after a CPU smoke (47 prompts, block 17, 257 neurons), before the full run (280 prompts, blocks 12, 17, 22, all 4,096 neurons each)
question: Gemini 4's transplant of Cammarata's Edge Featurizers figure (96 edge motifs vs 96 activation factors in ImageNet attribution graphs; median margin drop 0.86 vs 0.03 logits; usage-damage correlation median 0.35, teapot motif 0.80) to single language-model neurons: does edge consumption (how strongly downstream gates read a neuron's write) predict single-neuron ablation damage far better than node prominence (its write along the predicted token), and does it separate e568's bystander row (block 17, neuron 3002) from hubs?
design: Pythia-410m, e568's prompts at the last position (160 real and 60 invented countries in 'The capital of X is', 30 real and 30 invented people in 'The birthplace of X is'). Every neuron of blocks 12, 17, 22 scored, mean over prompts, by: projection (WDD's activation-free row score, the state after the block centred over the prompts on the unit write direction), activation |a|, write |a| |w_out|, node_u (Gemini's |a (w_out . u)|, u the unembedding of the model's top-1 token), node_direct (the exact first-order direct effect through the final LayerNorm), edge (Gemini's sum over downstream neurons of |a (w_out . w_in,k) phi'(h_k)|), edge_ln (the same through each block's LayerNorm), hop (the signed one-hop sum weighted by each downstream neuron's gradient), atp (|a dlogp/da|). Damage: each neuron zeroed at the last position (prefix cached), drop in log p of the model's own top-1 token, absolute, mean over prompts (primary); KL divergence (secondary). Spearman across neurons, 1,000-sample bootstrap over neurons for differences.

hypotheses.E1: Gemini's claim at block 17: rho(edge_ln) - rho(node_direct) >= 0.10 with the bootstrap 95% CI above 0 (SUPPORTED); CI above 0 but the difference below 0.10 (NARROWED); otherwise REFUTED. The literal pair (edge vs node_u) reported alongside, and blocks 12 and 22.
hypotheses.E2: the control Gemini's comparison lacks: at block 17, rho(edge_ln) - rho(write) >= 0.05 with the CI above 0, i.e. reading the downstream gates adds to the write's plain size
hypotheses.E3: gradient x activation is the best predictor of the absolute log-probability drop at every block, with rho >= 0.95 (one neuron at one position is nearly linear)
hypotheses.E4: the bystander: neuron 3002 of block 17 sits below the block's median on every activation-weighted score and on damage, and above the 95th percentile on the activation-free projection, over the invented-country prompts
